keyword: how long is the artemis 2 mission

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is designed as a roughly 10-day flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day mission" (R1, R2, R4, R5, R6, R7); "approximately 10 days" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All references describe the mission as a 10-day flight or approximately 10 days, directly supporting 'roughly 10-day'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is designed as approximately 9 days, 1 hour, and 46 minutes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "nine days, one hour and 46 minutes after liftoff" (R5, R6)
verifications.reasoning: R5 and R6 directly state the precise duration matching the claim.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission involves four astronauts traveling around the Moon and back to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts"... "around the moon" (R1); "four astronauts... orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission" (R2); similar in all
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm four astronauts on a mission flying around the Moon and returning to Earth.

verifications.claim: The four astronauts travel in the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Orion capsule is taking [four astronauts]" (R1); "Orion spacecraft" with crew (all others)
verifications.reasoning: Every reference explicitly states the four astronauts travel in Orion.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission tests systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "clear a path for... a new lunar landing" (R1); "pave the way for long-term exploration... lunar surface" (R2); "technological capability to send people to the Moon... preparations for new moon landings" (R3); "test Orion’s handling capabilities... for future missions with... lunar lander" (R4); "lay the foundation for an enduring presence on the Moon" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: References directly link mission tests to enabling future lunar landings and surface exploration.

verifications.claim: The goal of the Artemis 2 mission is a crewed flight test around the Moon to verify life-support and navigation systems.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey and keep its crew alive" (R1, life-support); "critical navigation and systems tests" (R3); "proximity operations... translunar injection" (R4, navigation); "check out Orion systems, including life support systems" (R6); "demonstrate life support systems" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Life-support explicitly supported; navigation implied via trajectory, prox ops, piloting tests but not always directly named.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 crew will enter a free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free-return trajectory" (R4, R6); "free-return trajectory" (R5); "translunar injection burn... harnessing lunar gravity to slingshot" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references explicitly name free-return trajectory.

verifications.claim: The free-return trajectory uses the gravity of both the Earth and Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free return trajectory. This path uses the moon’s gravity to swing the capsule directly back to Earth" (R1); "relies on the moon and Earth's gravity" (R5); "free-return trajectory around the moon" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm use of Earth and Moon gravity in free-return path.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 crew reaches their farthest point beyond the Moon on flight day 6.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Flight day 6: Lunar flyby... furthest from the Earth" (R4); "On flight day six, Orion will reach its farthermost point" (R5); "furthest point from Earth a little more than five days after liftoff" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by R4 and R5 as flight day 6; R6 aligns closely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 crew will not land on the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "around the moon but not land there" (R1); "orbit the Moon" no landing (R2); "will not land on the moon" (R3); flyby no landing (all)
verifications.reasoning: All references emphasize flyby/orbit around Moon without landing.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 crew will perform manual piloting tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Mr. Glover manually flew the spacecraft" (R1); "proximity operations... manual pilot demonstration" (R4, R7); "proximity operations demonstration... manual capabilities" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit mentions of manual flying and proximity operations tests.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 crew will spend about 3 hours in close proximity to the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "only spend about three hours on their closest pass of the moon's surface" (R4); "about three hours recording... during lunar flyby" (R4 again); lunar observations ~6 hours but 3 hours close (R5 context)
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly states about three hours during closest pass to lunar surface.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission concludes with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R1, R4, R5, R6); "splashdown... Pacific" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Consistent across references that it ends with Pacific splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is a precursor to the Artemis III landing mission.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "lunar spacesuit for the Artemis III mission" implying landing (R2); "Artemis III... will now focus on testing... first manned landing... Artemis IV" (R3 contradicts)
verifications.reasoning: R2 supports Artemis III as landing (suits); R3 explicitly states landing moved to Artemis IV, creating contradiction.
